title: UNITARES: Information-Theoretic Governance of Heterogeneous Agent Fleets
description:
UNITARES is a runtime governance layer for heterogeneous AI-agent fleets. It updates a four-dimensional state estimate x = (E, I, S, V)^T at each check-in and records governance interventions. We describe its February–April 2026 deployment, a class-conditional calibration protocol, and a migration method for changing reported coordinate semantics while preserving the existing decision path.

The proposed information-theoretic semantics are response-distribution entropy (S), context-response mutual information (I), negative variational free energy (E), and an accumulated free-energy residual (V). These are research targets: the reported deployment uses tier-3 heuristic estimators, and the specified logprob and multi-sample estimators remain unimplemented. Class-specific healthy operating points and manifold radii are measured for five agent classes; the remaining higher-tier scale constants are placeholders.

The empirical record includes a February 20 snapshot of 903 registered agents, 75 of them active, and a separate April 18 basin-label counterfactual on 13,310 state observations. Replacing the legacy tanh coherence with a class-conditional distance score changes 28.9% of basin assignments, predominantly into the low basin. The legacy score is nearly constant (about 0.49), and labels change where the replacement crosses classifier thresholds. This comparison changes both the formula and calibration; it does not isolate the value of class conditioning, replay the intervention pipeline, or establish which labels are correct. The surviving public export is a nearby pull (N = 13,292; 28.8% stored-label flips), not an exact archive of that table.

The migration mechanism orders decision-producing stages before presentation-producing enrichment. A corrected contraction certificate covers the printed fixed-parameter continuous vector field while trajectories remain in its stated domain and share exogenous inputs. It does not certify the implemented finite-step update or adaptive governor; an offline implementation counterexample illustrates this boundary. The paper establishes a framework and bounded descriptive results, not a validation of intervention quality or the proposed information-theoretic estimators.
notes: Version 6.9.4 (2026-10-13). Corrects the continuous contraction proof and states its fixed parameters, domain and common-input assumptions. Separates this certificate from the numerical update and adaptive governor; corrects stochastic, network, equilibrium and logistic claims. Includes an offline finite-step counterexample and reproducer. Also separates the coherence transform range from its observed concentration. Historical measurements are retained. The October 13 update corrects data access, discloses the nearby archived export, and distinguishes basin-label changes from intervention decisions.
